organizations.normalization_notes: Military assignment is modeled separately from civilian employment.
Rabassa's relationship is student status, not employment.
Professional affiliation establishes attorney status but is not an employer.

affiliations.research_notes: The official bar record documents admission and attorney status before wartime naval service. It does not name an employer or prove that legal work was Quirk's immediately preceding activity.
The U.S. Copyright Office biography says Rabassa enlisted in the Army in 1942 and served as an OSS cryptographer. The Army pathway is distinct from civilian employment.
Official and institutional biographies place Rabassa at Dartmouth before his 1942 Army enlistment. Dartmouth is student status, not an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Akeley P. Quirk is strongly matched to Akeley Park Quirk, a California attorney and retired U.S. Naval Reserve memoirist.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Recollections of World War II, by Akeley P Quirk, USNR (Ret)
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon name, P middle initial, naval status, and wartime memoir align with the indexed lieutenant commander.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match based on an exceptionally distinctive name plus consistent naval service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The 1935 bar admission predates the wartime naval and OSS context; it does not prove immediate pre-OSS employment.
claims.match_notes: No firm or employer is inferred from bar membership.

claims.claim_text: Akeley Park Quirk was admitted to the State Bar of California in May 1935 and had documented prewar attorney status.

claims.identity_match_assessment: The full middle name, uncommon name, and separate naval memoir citation support the indexed identity.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar professional status; immediacy to OSS service and any employing firm remain unknown.
claims.match_notes: Professional affiliation is not represented as employment.

claims.claim_text: Official Army and Library of Congress evidence support a high-confidence match between indexed Gregory L. Rabassa and the Dartmouth student who became an OSS cryptographer.
claims.evidence_excerpt: served as a cryptographer in North Africa and Italy
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and protected identifier agree, while the federal biography directly documents Army enlistment and OSS cryptographic service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match supported by two official sources and a distinctive full name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The biography places Dartmouth study before 1942 Army enlistment and OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The Army occupation code was not used; the role comes from the Library of Congress biography.

claims.claim_text: Gregory L. Rabassa's best-supported pathway into OSS was through the United States Army, which he joined in 1942.
claims.evidence_excerpt: enlisting in the Army in 1942. Within the Office of Strategic Services, he served as a cryptographer
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The federal biography explicitly sequences Army enlistment before service within OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact-name Army identifier match corroborated by an official federal biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded military pathway; it is not civilian employment.
claims.match_notes: The source does not name a pre-OSS Army unit, so none is invented.

claims.claim_text: Gregory L. Rabassa studied romance languages at Dartmouth College before his 1942 Army enlistment.
claims.evidence_excerpt: He studied romance languages at Dartmouth College before enlisting in the Army in 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The U.S. Copyright Office explicitly places Dartmouth study before Army service; Dartmouth's profile corroborates his student chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The distinctive full name and explicit OSS biography align with the indexed person.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar student affiliation, not the immediate military predecessor and not an employer.
claims.match_notes: Student attendance remains separate from employment analytics.
